title: Paid by a related organization as well as, or instead of, the one the City pays
question: Which officers and key employees of City-paid organizations report pay from a related organization in the same year, and how much comes from each?
finding: 320 current officers, directors and key employees at 33 City-paid organizations were reported as receiving $10,000 or more from a related organization in at least one year (681 person-years); 260 were paid by the filing organization as well in their latest year and 60 only by the related one. 34% of them are at three organizations: Adventist Health St Helena (44), Dignity Health Dba St Mary's Medical Ctr (33) and California Pacific Medical Center (32). Where the City supplied a quarter or more of the filer’s revenue there are 40 at 9 organizations: the best paid is Kenneth Lombard, President of Bridge Regional Partners Inc, with $1.1 million from related organizations and $45,067 from the organization itself in the year ended 31 December 2024.
how: From Part VII of every return on file: reportable compensation from related organizations of $10,000 or more for a current officer, director, trustee or key employee, beside the same person’s pay from the filing organization. One row for each person and organization, showing the latest year, with the number of years in which it occurs. Ranked with organizations for which the City supplied at least 25% of revenue that year first, then by total pay. The return does not say which related organization paid. Where the organization’s tax number was matched by hand and has not been verified, the last column says so.
limits: This is how groups of related nonprofits are normally run: a parent or management affiliate employs the leadership and each affiliate’s return reports the same people with their pay shown as coming from the related body. The same pay then appears on several returns and must not be added up across them. It matters to a funder for one reason only: where the executive is paid elsewhere, the City-paid entity’s own payroll and its budget to the City do not show the cost of its leadership, or show it as a management fee. Whether the split of time and cost is fair is a question for the agreements between the related bodies.
